overall_three_extension_readiness_status.human_summary: All three extensions still have unclosed blockers or partial-only evidence. Claude and Codex require user-host action to expose safe live/user-visible routes. Cursor remains partial because same-Row23 visible UI and nonhost readiness gates are not closed.

Claude: Approve or provide a no-secret Claude live-host route. Acceptable next proof route must either start Claude Code with the session-local plugin and prove SessionStart/local hook execution without submitting a prompt externally, or explicitly authorize submitting the approved Row23 safe prompt through Claude --print/chat with redacted I/O and no secrets. Without that approval/route, live-host status remains BLOCKED.
Cursor: Open or restore the Cursor Extension Development Host window for XIIGen Smart Skills.
Close or hide the Cursor Agent/chat pane, or provide a separate local-only XIIGen Smart Skills panel route where no external AI chat input is visible or focusable.
Expose the local XIIGen panel input/command target for the approved Row23 prompt and confirm no secrets are present.
Then authorize a bounded worker to run focus preflight and screenshot metadata first; same-Row23 visible submission can proceed only if the target is proven local-only and not Cursor Agent/chat.
Codex: Expose one safe, user-visible Codex route to a bounded worker, then rerun CODEX-HOST-UI-ROUTE-PROOF for Row23. Acceptable routes: an already-open in-app Browser tab to the Codex host/plugin/thread page that the worker can claim; a callable Codex app/thread/host automation tool exposed to the worker; or a fixed Codex CLI/plugin command route that executes without Access denied. Continue to forbid secrets, external AI prompt submission outside Row23 authority, network installs, and git.
